tb-01.note: Opposites. 입원 means being admitted to hospital (병원에 입원해요), while 퇴원 means leaving hospital after getting well (건강해져서 퇴원해요).
Both mean habit. 버릇 often refers to personal quirks or unconscious habits (손톱을 깨무는 버릇), while 습관 is broader and neutral (좋은 독서 습관).
들리다 means to be heard by ears (노랫소리가 들려요), and also to drop by a place briefly (서점에 잠시 들러요).

tb-02.note: Opposites. 오른손 means the right hand (오른손을 들어요), while 왼손 means the left hand (왼손으로 글씨를 써요).
손가락 means finger on a hand (열 손가락), while 발가락 means toe on a foot (발가락이 아파요).
낫다 means to recover from illness (감기가 다 나았어요), and also to be better than another choice (이 옷이 더 나아요).

tb-03.note: Opposites. 늘다 means to increase or improve (실력이 늘어요), while 줄다 means to decrease or shrink (체중이 줄어요).
열리다 means a door opens (문이 열려요), fruit grows on a tree (열매가 열려요), and an event is held (축제가 열려요).
Opposites. 오래되다 means aged or used for a long time (오래된 건물), while 새롭다 means new or fresh (새로운 느낌).

tb-04.note: Opposites. 올리다 means to raise or lift up (손을 올려요), while 내리다 means to lower or drop down (손을 내려요).
Opposites. 강하다 means strong or sturdy (바람이 강해요), while 약하다 means weak or frail (몸이 약해요).
Opposites. 줄이다 means to reduce or shorten (시간을 줄여요), while 늘리다 means to increase or expand (양을 늘려요).

tb-05.note: Opposites. 이상 means or more / above (열 살 이상), while 이하 means or less / below (십만 원 이하).
Opposites. 비다 means to be empty (방이 비어 있어요), while 차다 means to be full (자리가 다 찼어요).
Opposites. 충분하다 means enough or ample (시간이 충분해요), while 부족하다 means insufficient or lacking (잠이 부족해요).

tb-06.note: Opposites. 일부 means a part or portion (일부 학생), while 전부 means all or entirety (전부 다 했어요).
Opposites in math. 더하다 means to add (숫자를 더해요), while 빼다 means to subtract or remove (살을 빼요, 삼을 빼요).
대 is a counter for vehicles and machines (차 두 대, 컴퓨터 세 대), and also denotes age groups (이십대 청년).

tb-07.note: Opposites. 겉 means the outside surface (겉은 바삭해요), while 속 means the inner part or inside (속은 따뜻해요).
Both mean surroundings or nearby vicinity. 주변 (학교 주변) and 주위 (집 주위) are very commonly interchangeable.
Opposites. 가까이 means near or close (가까이 오세요), while 멀리 means far away (멀리 떠나요).

tb-08.note: Opposites. 굵다 means thick for round cylindrical items (나무가 굵어요), while 가늘다 means thin or slender (실이 가늘어요).
Opposites. 하얗다 means pure white (눈이 하얘요), while 까맣다 means deep black (머리카락이 까매요).
줄 means a rope or line to stand in (줄을 서요), and also the grammar form for knowing how to do (피아노를 칠 줄 알아요).

tb-09.note: Major Korean traditional holidays. 설날 is Lunar New Year in winter (떡국을 먹어요), while 추석 is harvest festival in autumn (송편을 먹어요).
Both mean green color. 초록색 is native-style and very common in conversation, while 녹색 is Sino-Korean (녹색 불이 켜져요).
Opposites. 얇다 means thin for flat items like paper or clothes (책이 얇아요), while 두껍다 means thick (두꺼운 옷).

tb-10.note: Pronounced the same. 매다 means to tie or fasten (넥타이를 매요, 끈을 매요), while 메다 means to carry on one's shoulder (가방을 메요).
입다 means to put on clothes (옷을 입어요), while 갈아입다 means to change clothes (잠옷으로 갈아입어요).
목걸이 is a necklace worn around the neck (예쁜 목걸이), while 귀걸이 is an earring worn on ears (귀걸이를 해요).

tb-11.note: Opposites. 반바지 means shorts (여름에 반바지를 입어요), while 긴바지 means trousers or long pants (긴바지를 입어요).
Opposites. 현금 means cash paper or coins (현금으로 내요), while 카드는 means a credit or bank card (카드로 결제해요).
Opposites. 동전 means metal coins (백 원짜리 동전), while 지폐 means paper bills (만 원짜리 지폐).

tb-12.note: Both mean free of charge. 공짜 is everyday colloquial Korean (공짜로 얻었어요), while 무료 is formal Sino-Korean (무료 입장).
Opposites. 서다 means to stand up (자리에 서 있어요), while 앉다 means to sit down (의자에 앉아요).
Opposites. 잊다 means to forget (약속을 잊었어요), while 기억하다 means to remember (이름을 기억해요).

tb-13.note: 감다 means to close one's eyes (눈을 감아요), to wash one's hair (머리를 감아요), and to wind rope or bandages.
Opposites. 묶다 means to tie or knot (신발 끈을 묶어요), while 풀다 means to untie or solve (끈을 풀어요, 문제를 풀어요).
Opposites. 잃어버리다 means to lose an item (지갑을 잃어버렸어요), while 찾다 means to find it (지갑을 찾았어요).

tb-14.note: Opposites on doors. 밀다 means to push forward (문을 밀어요), while 당기다 means to pull backward (문을 당겨요).
뜨다 means to open eyes (눈을 떠요), to float on water (배가 떠요), and for the sun or moon to rise (해가 떠요).
Opposites. 넣다 means to put inside (가방에 책을 넣어요), while 꺼내다 means to pull out (가방에서 책을 꺼내요).

tb-15.note: Opposites. 줍다 means to pick up from the floor (쓰레기를 주워요), while 버리다 means to throw away (쓰레기를 버려요).
Opposites. 펴다 means to unfold or open (우산을 펴요, 책을 펴요), while 접다 means to fold up (우산을 접어요).
Opposites. 틀다 means to turn on water or an appliance (물을 틀어요, 라디오를 틀어요), while 끄다 means to turn it off.

tb-16.note: Opposites. 평일 means weekdays Monday to Friday (평일에 출근해요), while 주말 means the weekend Saturday and Sunday (주말에 쉬어요).
Opposites. 과거 means the past (과거의 추억), while 현재 means the present time (현재 살고 있는 집).
곧 means soon in the coming moments (기차가 곧 와요), while 방금 means just a moment ago in the past (방금 도착했어요).

tb-17.note: 자주 means often or frequently (자주 만나요), while 가끔 means sometimes or occasionally (가끔 영화를 봐요).
Korean day counters. 이틀 means two days (이틀 동안), while 사흘 means three days (사흘 동안; not four days!).
Opposites. 첫 means the very first placed before a noun (첫 만남), while 마지막 means the final or last (마지막 수업).

tb-18.note: Opposites. 연초 means the start of the year (연초 계획), while 연말 means the close of the year (연말 파티).
Opposites. 이전 means before or earlier than a set time (오후 세 시 이전), while 이후 means after that time (세 시 이후).
밤 means nighttime while it is dark (밤 10시), while 새벽 means dawn or the quiet hours before sunrise (새벽 5시).

tb-19.note: Opposites for temperature. 영상 means above freezing zero degrees (영상 15도), while 영하 means sub-zero (영하 8도).
Opposites. 얼다 means to freeze into ice (물이 얼어요), while 녹다 means to melt or thaw (얼음이 녹아요).
Opposites. 익숙하다 means familiar or used to something (길이 익숙해요), while 낯설다 means unfamiliar (낯선 동네).

tb-20.note: 심심하다 means feeling bored with nothing to do (할 일이 없어서 심심해요), while 지루하다 means tedious from taking too long (수업이 지루해요).
화 means anger or fury (화가 나요, 화를 내요), and also fire or disaster (화재).
Opposites. 행복 means happiness or joy (행복을 느껴요), while 불행 means misfortune or sorrow (불행을 이겨내요).

tb-21.note: Opposites. 울음 means crying or weeping (울음을 터뜨려요), while 웃음 means laughter or a smile (웃음이 나와요).
Opposites. 시끄럽다 means noisy or loud (밖이 시끄러워요), while 조용하다 means quiet and calm (방이 조용해요).
꿈 means a dream while sleeping (어젯밤 꿈을 꿨어요), and also a future goal or wish (선생님이 저의 꿈이에요).

tb-22.note: 깎다 means to peel fruit with a knife (사과를 깎아요), and also to discount or bargain a price (값을 깎아 주세요).
끓다 is intransitive (물이 끓어요 = the water boils), while 끓이다 is transitive (냄비에 라면을 끓여요 = I boil ramen).
굽다 means to roast or bake food (고기를 구워요, 빵을 구워요), and also to be curved or bent (허리가 굽었어요).

tb-23.note: Both mean chicken egg. 달걀 is native Korean (달걀을 삶아요), while 계란 is Sino-Korean (계란을 풀어요). Both are completely interchangeable.
찌다 means to steam food (만두를 쪄요), to gain body weight (살이 쪘어요), and for summer weather to feel sweltering.
소고기 means beef from a cow (소고기 볶음), while 돼지고기 means pork from a pig (돼지고기 김치찌개).

tb-24.note: Both mean vegetables. 채소 is standard Korean for cultivated greens (신선한 채소), while 야채 is also widely used in daily conversation (야채를 씻어요).
수저 refers to the combination pair of spoon and chopsticks together (수저를 놓아요), while 숟가락 is just the spoon.
Opposites in cuisine. 한식 means Korean food (된장찌개와 밥), while 양식 means Western-style meals (스파게티와 샐러드).

tb-25.note: Opposites. 찬물 means cold water (찬물을 마셔요), while 더운물 means hot or warm water (더운물로 손을 씻어요).
녹차 is unfermented green tea (따뜻한 녹차를 마셔요), while 홍차 is fermented black tea (향긋한 홍차).
닭고기 refers to raw or cooked chicken meat as an ingredient (닭고기 수프), while 치킨 specifically refers to crispy fried chicken (치킨을 주문해요).

tb-26.note: 김 means dried edible seaweed sheets (김에 밥을 싸요), and also hot steam rising from soup (김이 모락모락 나요).
쌀 is uncooked raw rice grains before cooking (쌀을 씻어요), while 밥 is cooked edible rice ready to eat (밥을 먹어요).
Opposites in seasoning. 설탕 is sweet sugar (설탕을 넣어요), while 소금 is salty salt (소금으로 간을 맞춰요).

tb-27.note: Opposites for drinks or color. 진하다 means strong or dark (진한 커피, 진한 색), while 연하다 means mild or pale (연한 보리차, 연한 색).
등 means the back of a person's body (등이 아파요), an electric light or lamp (가로등), and etc. in lists (사과, 배 등).
장 is the counter for thin flat sheets like paper or tickets (종이 한 장, 표 두 장), and also means a chapter in a book.

tb-28.note: Pronounced identically as [부치다]. 붙이다 means to stick or paste (벽에 사진을 붙여요), while 부치다 means to send a letter by post (편지를 부쳐요).
켤레 is the counter for pairs of shoes or socks (신발 한 켤레), while 벌 is the counter for sets of clothing (옷 두 벌).
Both mean we or our. 우리 is standard (우리 학교), while 저희 is the polite humble pronoun used when speaking to elders (저희 가족).

tb-29.note: Both mean laundry. 빨래 is everyday native Korean (빨래를 널어요), while 세탁 is Sino-Korean used in words like 세탁기 (세탁을 해요).
선풍기 is an electric fan with spinning blades (선풍기를 틀어요), while 에어컨 is a refrigeration air conditioner (에어컨을 켜요).
옷장 is a wardrobe for hanging clothes (옷장에 옷을 걸어요), while 책장 is a bookcase for holding books (책장에 책을 꽂아요).

tb-30.note: 초 means a wax candle (촛불을 켜요), a second of clock time (십 초 동안), and the beginning of a period (학기 초).
짓다 means to construct a house (집을 지어요), to cook rice (밥을 지어요), to smile (미소를 지어요), or to give a name (이름을 지어요).
Opposites. 지하 means underground or basement level (지하철, 지하 1층), while 지상 means above ground (지상 주차장).
